title: Basics
description: Behavioral and personal interview questions with adaptable first-person model answers.

questions.question: Tell me about yourself.
questions.sampleAnswer: I have been a web developer for the past 4 years, building web and mobile apps. I commonly work with Vue.js, Typescript, Laravel, MySQL, GraphQL, and REST APIs, and I pick up other tools when a project needs them. I also do graphic and UI/UX design, so I can take project from first design through to a working app or website.
followUps: Can you go deeper into that project result?

questions.question: What is your expected salary?
questions.sampleAnswer: Based on my research and current market rates for this role, I'm looking for a monthly salary of P0 to P0. That range reflects my skills and experience.
hints: State a range, not a single rigid number.
followUps: What factors matter beyond base pay?

questions.question: Why do you want this role?
questions.sampleAnswer: I want this role because it fits the work I already do. I build web & mobile apps and I also do UI design. I can take projects/features from design to working product.
followUps: How does this compare with your current role?
questions.voicePrompt: Why are you interested in this role?

questions.question: Tell me about a conflict with a teammate and how you handled it.
questions.sampleAnswer: In [project], a teammate and I disagreed on implementation priority, and delivery risk was rising. I scheduled a focused discussion where we listed assumptions, constraints, and impact on users instead of debating preferences. We aligned on a phased approach: first a safe baseline, then optimization in a second step. The conflict resolved quickly, and we delivered on time with better trust in the team.
followUps: What did you learn from that conflict?
questions.voicePrompt: Describe a teammate conflict you resolved.

questions.question: Where do you see yourself in 5 years?
questions.sampleAnswer: In five years, I see myself as a strong [role level] who can lead complex initiatives end-to-end and mentor teammates effectively. I want to deepen my expertise in [technical area] while growing my product and communication skills. My goal is to contribute at both code and system level, helping teams ship reliably and make better long-term decisions.
hints: Keep goals aligned with the role.
followUps: What skills are you building now for that path?
questions.voicePrompt: Where do you see yourself in five years?

questions.question: Why should we hire you?
questions.sampleAnswer: You should hire me because I combine hands-on delivery with reliable communication across engineering and stakeholders. I have experience in [relevant domain], and I have consistently delivered outcomes like [specific metric or project]. I ramp up quickly, ask strong clarifying questions, and stay accountable for quality after release. I believe that combination would let me add value to your team early.
followUps: What is one impact you can make in your first 90 days?

questions.question: Tell me about a mistake you made and what you learned.
questions.sampleAnswer: Early in [project], I underestimated testing effort and we found bugs late in the release cycle. I took responsibility, coordinated a focused fix plan, and worked with QA to prioritize risk-based coverage. After that release, I introduced earlier test checkpoints and clearer definition-of-done criteria. The main lesson was to plan validation as part of delivery, not as a final step.
followUps: How did your team process change afterward?
questions.voicePrompt: Share a mistake and what you learned.

questions.question: How do you work with cross-functional teams?
questions.sampleAnswer: I align early on goals, constraints, and decision timelines so engineering, product, and design have shared expectations. During execution I communicate status and risks in plain language, then escalate blockers before they become schedule issues. I also document key decisions so new context does not get lost. This approach helps teams move faster without sacrificing quality.
followUps: How do you handle shifting priorities?

questions.question: How do you handle tight deadlines?
questions.sampleAnswer: When deadlines are tight, I first clarify non-negotiables and split work into must-have versus nice-to-have scope. I focus execution on highest impact tasks, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and keep frequent check-ins so surprises are surfaced early. I also protect quality on critical paths by keeping basic testing and rollback plans in place. That balance helps me deliver quickly without creating avoidable rework.
followUps: When would you push back on deadline commitments?
questions.voicePrompt: How do you perform under deadline pressure?

questions.question: What questions would you ask the interviewer?
questions.sampleAnswer: I would ask what success looks like in the first 90 days, which current team challenges are most urgent, and how engineering decisions are made across product and design. I would also ask how feedback and growth are supported for this role. These questions help me understand expectations, collaboration style, and whether I can contribute effectively in your environment.
hints: Ask about role clarity and impact.
followUps: Why do these questions matter to you?
questions.voicePrompt: What questions would you ask us?
